account:
It is day 1, just after 13:00, and I have returned to town hall for council letters. My morning mill inspection ran late. I inspected the mill stall and found 74 hay bales, so that stock showed no evident shortage, though I did not establish the condition of all the mill's stores.

The unusual thing is a stream of vague reports about a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, innkeeper, freight and neighbour as people present in different accounts. One also reported the baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not witnessed a change to a crossing or heard a concrete proposal from an organiser. I crossed the bridge this morning. When I asked the neighbour, they likewise knew only vague reports and suggested asking the baker directly. These reports may all be repetitions of the same uncertain news rather than independent confirmation. I do not yet know whether anything is actually being arranged, or what it would be for.

There is also a confirmed addition to my schedule: an 18:00 great-hall lighting inspection with the builder and secretary, to check eight installed lanterns and lighting around four tables. The appointment addendum says I approved it yesterday. The innkeeper has agreed to join a 17:30 meeting here with the secretary and builder before that inspection. The builder is now waiting near the hall entrance. This could simply be ordinary arrangements for the inspection; I have no evidence connecting it to the bakery rumours or to some other purpose.

I want to keep my appointments while getting first-hand clarification rather than encouraging speculation. The secretary is nearby, and council correspondence is my immediate business. Tea with the neighbour at 15:00 is another opportunity to hear whether anything definite has emerged.
